L265: 
L266: 【94†`bc49dcd`】
L267: ### Changed
L268: 
L269:   * Raise the dependency floors to apcore 0.32.0 and apcore-toolkit 0.14.0.
L270: Python's `openapi` extra uses the same toolkit floor.
L271:   * Align runtime declarations with upstream requirements: Node.js 20+ and
L272: Rust 1.86+. Update the TypeScript CI Node version accordingly.
L273: ### Fixed
L274:   * Render input validation diagnostics from apcore's canonical
L275: `details.errors` entries (`path`, `keyword`, `message`). Preserve RFC 6901
L276: JSON Pointers, including nested indices and escaped property names, and
L277: display the empty root pointer as `<root>`. Free-form diagnostic messages
L278: still pass through path/traceback sanitization and the combined message is
L279: limited to 500 characters. Output/config failures remain internal errors;
L280: errors without canonical diagnostics retain the sanitized original message.
L281:   * Extend the shared error-mapping conformance driver to exercise structured
L282: diagnostics instead of synthesizing field names into the error message.
L283: ### Compatibility
L284:   * Toolkit 0.14.0 tightens binding-file validation (unknown keys, incomplete
L285: schema pairs and strict-mode tags). The A2A backend does not use that loader;
L286: its OpenAPI scanner, registry writer and reference resolver need no API change.
L287: Deployments that load bindings separately must move custom entry keys into
L288: `metadata`, supply both inline schemas, and use list-valued `tags`.
L289:   * Core 0.32.0's governance, cancellation, redaction and registration fixes are
L290: inherited through the existing executor/registry APIs. No A2A wire-code or
L291: OpenAPI skill-ID migration is required for this update.

L324: 【96†python/v0.8.1】
L325: 
L326: 【97†`c4bb4b4`】
L327: 
L328: Adopts apcore-toolkit 0.13.0, whose `OpenAPIScanner` now emits every `module_id` in apcore's
L329: Canonical ID alphabet itself, and retires this binding's own module-ID projection (FR-OAS-002)
L330: to match. Tracks the `apcore-a2a` spec's `openapi_backend.json` contract 2.0.
L331: Suite: 479 tests (was 467), 7 skipped, `ruff check` / `ruff format --check` clean.
L332: ### Changed — BREAKING
L333:   * OpenAPI-derived module IDs — and therefore A2A skill IDs — change for every camelCase or
L334: hyphenated `operationId` and path. The toolkit splits camelCase into snake_case words where
L335: this binding's projection only lowercased: `listPets` → `list_pets` (was `listpets`); under
L336: `prefix: petstore`, `petstore.list_pets` (was `petstore.listpets`); and camelCase path
L337: parameters likewise (`GET /pets/{petId}` → `pets.pet_id.get`, was `pets.petid.get`). A
L338: `prefix` is normalised with the rest of the ID (`Pet-Store` → `pet_store.…`). IDs that were
L339: already lowercase and legal are unchanged. Migration: ACL rules (`targets`), bindings, and
L340: `include` / `exclude` patterns keyed on the old IDs must be updated — the scanner's filters
L341: match the emitted, normalised ID (`^read_audit_log$`, not `readAuditLog`). The recommended
L342: prefixed catch-all deny rule (`petstore.*`) keeps holding, but an allow-list of old operation
L343: names now fails closed until it is updated. Clients that call skills by ID must use the new IDs.
L344:   * Required `apcore-toolkit` floor raised to 0.13.0 (was `>=0.12.0`), both the base
L345: dependency and the `openapi` extra.
L346:   * FR-OAS-002 is now a skip policy, applied after `scan`. The backend no longer rewrites IDs:
L347: it registers the ID the scanner emitted. It still skips a module whose emitted ID apcore's
L348: registry would reject — the one case the toolkit deliberately does not repair, a segment that
L349: begins with a digit (`/v1/2fa` → `v1.2fa.get`), or an empty ID from a hook — with the same
L350: WARNING as before, now checked on the IDs `scan` returns instead of inside `transform_module`.
L351: A hook returning `MyThing` is normalised by the toolkit to `my_thing` and registers (the old
L352: in-hook projection made it `mything`; a legality check left there would have skipped it). The
L353: toolkit's own legality warning for a skipped module is not re-emitted beside the skip line.
L354:   * The FR-OAS-003 description repair runs on the modules `scan` returns, still after the
L355: caller's `transform_module` hook, so the synthesis INFO line names the IDs actually emitted —
L356: including a deduplicated `…_2`, which the in-hook repair, running before the scanner's
L357: deduplication, reported under the pre-deduplication ID (`list_pets` twice, never
L358: `list_pets_2`).
L359: ### Deprecated
L360: 
L361:   * `project_module_id`. apcore-toolkit >= 0.13 emits IDs in apcore's alphabet, so the
L362: projection is no longer needed and nothing in this package calls it. It keeps its behaviour and
L363: now emits a `DeprecationWarning` on every call; it will be removed in a later minor release. It
L364: does not reproduce the toolkit's naming (`listPets` → `listpets`, not `list_pets`), so do not
L365: use it to predict the ID a module registers under. `MODULE_ID_SEGMENT` is unaffected — the skip
L366: policy uses it.
L367: ### Fixed
L368:   * An operation removed by `include` / `exclude` was still reported as description-synthesized.
L369: The repair ran inside the scanner's `transform_module` hook, which runs before the scanner's
L370: own filters, so the FR-OAS-003 INFO line named operations that never registered and counted
L371: them against a denominator that excluded them (measured on 0.8.0: `2 of 1 scanned operations … Affected: listpets, secret` with `exclude="secret"`). The feature spec already required the
L372: opposite ("an operation excluded by configuration is never synthesized for and never
L373: reported"); running the repair after `scan` makes it true.
L374: ### Tests
L375:   * The conformance driver reads `openapi_backend.json` contract 2.0: re-pinned IDs; three new
L376: cases (`projection_hook_output_normalised_not_skipped`,
L377: `description_synthesis_report_names_the_emitted_id`,
L378: `description_not_synthesized_for_excluded_operation`); the fixture's named `hooks` (an unknown
L379: hook name fails the case); `expected_no_error_logs`; `expected_synthesis_report`; and the
L380: per-module `warnings_contain`, which this driver previously did not assert.
L381:   * New regressions: the backend never calls `project_module_id`; an illegal hook-returned ID is
L382: skipped whatever its shape (including the empty ID); a skipped module reaches no later
L383: diagnostic (no synthesis, no FR-OAS-005 count, the zero-modules warning fires, nothing at
L384: ERROR); a caller hook's `Pet-Store.ListPets` registers as `pet_store.list_pets` with its
L385: cleared description repaired.

L418: 【99†python/v0.8.0】
L419: 
L420: 【100†`cf17ff2`】
L421: 
L422: Minor release, version-aligned with the TypeScript and Rust SDKs. Raises the required floor to
L423: `apcore>=0.31.0` / `apcore-toolkit>=0.12.0` and fixes a `global_deadline` regression found while
L424: reviewing what those two releases changed.
L425: 
L426: Suite: 467 tests (was 449), 7 skipped, `ruff check` clean.
L427: ### Fixed
L428:   * `ApCoreAgentExecutor` passed `global_deadline` as a `time.monotonic()` value; apcore >= 0.31.0
L429: requires epoch seconds (`time.time()`). apcore's own `Context.create` contract was always
L430: documented as `time.time() + budget` (PROTOCOL_SPEC), but apcore-python's internal enforcement
L431: compared the deadline against `time.monotonic()` until 0.31.0 (apcore D-99) — against that bug, a
L432: spec-conformant epoch-seconds deadline is ~1.8e9 versus a ~1e5 monotonic clock, so it silently
L433: never fired (fail-open, no budget enforced at all). This executor worked around apcore's bug by
L434: deliberately passing a monotonic value instead of the documented one, with a comment recording
L435: the reason ("matching apcore BuiltinContextStep"). apcore 0.31.0 fixes its own comparison to
L436: match the documented contract, which flips the failure mode: a monotonic value now reads as
L437: already-expired against `time.time()`, so every module call would fail immediately. Fixed to pass
L438: `time.time() + execution_timeout`, per the documented contract apcore now actually honors. New
L439: regression test: `tests/server/test_executor.py::test_execute_passes_epoch_seconds_global_deadline`.
L440: Found by grepping this package's apcore-facing code against the apcore 0.31.0 changelog, the same
L441: process that found the D-103 identity-synthesis divergence in `apcore-a2a-rust`'s `acl_context()`
L442: (apcore-python was never affected by D-103 — `card_visibility.py::_acl_context` already delegated
L443: identity handling straight to `Context.create`, with no manual synthesis of its own).
L444: ### Changed — dependency floor
L445:   * Required `apcore` floor raised to 0.31.0 (was `>=0.30.0`) and required `apcore-toolkit`
L446: floor raised to 0.12.0 (was `>=0.11.1`, both the base dependency and the `openapi` extra).
L447: apcore 0.31.0 is two joined audit cycles (`PROTOCOL_SPEC` v1.37.0 → v1.59.0) settling 54
L448: cross-language divergences, five of them security defects. Beyond the `global_deadline` fix
L449: above, every other `apcore.*`/`apcore_toolkit.*` surface this package uses was checked against
L450: both changelogs' breaking-change sections and needs no change:
L451:   * `governance_state()` (`server/factory.py`, `openapi_backend.py`) — apcore 0.31.0's D-125 union
L452: fix is internal to apcore's own gate; this package only reads the result.
L453:   * `ACL.check_access` (`adapters/card_visibility.py`) — unaffected; D-96/D-97's approval-bypass
L454: union fix is internal to apcore's gate, not the `check_access` contract.
L455:   * `apcore_toolkit.deep_resolve_refs` (`adapters/schema.py`) — fully delegates $ref resolution to
L456: the shared toolkit helper, which got the $ref-sibling-key security fix (the same defect class as
L457: apcore's D-98/D-124) directly in 0.12.0; this package has no independent ref-resolution or
L458: redaction logic of its own to carry the same bug (contrast `apcore-mcp-python`, which had an
L459: independent `_inline_refs` with the identical latent bug, fixed in its own 0.22.0).
L460:   * `sys_modules` per-group registration (`server/factory.py`) — apcore 0.31.0 makes the four
L461: per-group `sys_modules.*.enabled` flags actually enforced (previously ignored), but
L462: `apcore.sys_modules.registration.register_sys_modules` supplies `True` as its own explicit
L463: default for each when absent from the `Config`, so this package's `Config(data=sys_data)` call
L464: (which only sets the top-level `sys_modules.enabled`) is unaffected.
L465:   * No usage of `ContextFactory.create_context` (D-76), `TaskStoreError` (D-92, falls through this
L466: package's generic "unknown apcore error code" handler safely either way), `Context.logger`
L467: (deprecated), `ExtensionManager` (D-78), registry event subscriptions (D-80), or `BindingLoader`
L468: (toolkit).
L469:   * The monorepo-root `uv.lock` already resolved `apcore` and `apcore-toolkit` to 0.31.0/0.12.0 via
L470: their workspace-editable local paths before this change (workspace sources bypass the version
L471: specifier in `requires-dist` entirely), so it needed no regeneration. This package has no lock
L472: file of its own.

L507: 【103†`fefbb98`】
L508: 
L509: Minor release, version-aligned with the TypeScript and Rust SDKs. Ships the OpenAPI
L510: Backend (feature F-12) and raises the required floor to `apcore>=0.30.0` /
L511: `apcore-toolkit>=0.11.1` — which is the same change, since apcore-toolkit 0.11.0 is what
L512: shipped the OpenAPI Scanner the feature is built on.
L513: Suite: 449 tests (was 392), 7 skipped, `ruff check` clean.
L514: ### Added
L515: 
L516:   * `apcore_a2a.openapi_backend` — `openapi_backend()`, plus `project_module_id`,
L517: `resolve_spec_location`, `synthesize_description` and
L518: `build_openapi_backend_from_config`. Point it at an OpenAPI 3.0/3.1 document and every
